## Soft Metadata

> [!WARNING]
> **Tier 2 (community estimate)** — Soft Metadata below adapted from publisher-disclosed practices (apa.org/pubs/journals/hea) and community-aggregator evidence (editage, APA statistics) gathered 2026-05. Submission practitioners are invited to upgrade individual claims to Tier 1 via `/ja-validate`. See [SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md](../../../../SEED_DATA_QUALITY.md) for the Skeleton → Tier 2 → Tier 1 lifecycle.

> **The core value of this entry.** OpenAlex cannot fill any of these — they require lived experience and community knowledge. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](../../../../CONTRIBUTING.md) for guidance.

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | High — international health-psychology authorship |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | Medium |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Very High — health disparities, minority-stress, intersectional health |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Health psychology + behavioral medicine — health behavior change, chronic illness, stress/coping, intervention research |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **health-psychology contribution** with empirical methodology. EIC Kenneth E. Freedland leads APA Division 38.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Initial editorial evaluation may result in rejection without external peer review (community evidence: apa.org/pubs/journals/hea 2026-05). Average 2–3 months to first decision.

|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core — RCTs, longitudinal |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | Mixed-methods only |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | With empirical implications |
| Mixed methods | 4 | Common in health psychology |
| Meta-analysis | 5 | Welcomed |

Reviewers from APA Division 38 (Health Psychology) and broader behavioral-medicine community. Single-masked review (community evidence: apa.org 2026-05). Common demands: "Health outcome significance?", "Mechanism?", "Intervention fidelity?", "Disparities consideration?".

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts without health-psychology framing
- Pure qualitative without mixed-methods backing
- AI use without disclosure per APA policy

### Soft Tax

Low for health-psychology empirical authors. Moderate for adjacent psychology — requires health-outcome framing. 2–3 month decision cycle is reasonable.

### Best Suited For

- Chronic illness management research
- Health behavior change studies
- Stress / coping research
- Health disparities work
- Behavioral medicine RCTs
- Meta-analyses of health-intervention literatures

### Not Recommended For

- Pure clinical psychology (consider JCCP)
- Pure autoethnography
- Theoretical-only without empirical test

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology](./journal-of-consulting-and-clinical-psychology.md) | If treatment-focused; APA family |
| 2 | [Journal of Occupational Health Psychology](./journal-of-occupational-health-psychology.md) | If workplace-health focused; APA family |
| 3 | *(Journal of Behavioral Medicine — community contribution welcome to map fallback)* | If behavioral-medicine specialty |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from a top behavioral-medicine venue as "too psychology-focused," Health Psychology is often a better fit — APA Division 38 audience, behavior-change frameworks native.
